..
Friday through Friday night: Zonal upper level flow behind a
weak shortwave pulse will maintain a warm, dry pattern through
tonight. Daytime highs will reach the 80s as onshore flow pushes
westerly winds through the Cascade gaps this evening similar to
the previous few days.

Saturday (Independence Day): A flattening shortwave trough
moving onshore into British Columbia will cause a weak cold
front to move into the Pacific NW, with downstream ridging
amplifying across the Rockies. This will cause very dry, gusty
winds to blow across central to eastern WA Saturday. RH values 
will bottom out in the 15-25% range in the afternoon with gusts 
of 25-35mph, supporting areas of critical fire weather 
conditions. Given this setup and the elevated potential for 
ignitions with Independence Day celebrations, have gone ahead 
and upgraded the Watch to Red Flag Warnings for much of this 
area Saturday. Funneling winds down the Okanogan & Methow 
Valleys, as well as downsloping off the Blue Mountains should 
also lead to similarly critical winds and low RHs, so have 
included these areas in the RFW as well. Far eastern WA and to a
lesser extent northern ID will see elevated fire weather 
conditions given the breezy winds, though critical thresholds 
are not expected to be met.

Saturday night: Decreasing PWAT anomalies across the region will
hamper RH recoveries to a degree Saturday night, though still
average in 'Fair' (55-75%) territory for most areas. Portions 
of Okanogan Valley may only see RH recoveries in the 40-55% 
range with a breezy funnel of northerly winds into the valley. 
Will continue to monitor as this may continue the locally 
elevated fire weather concerns in the region overnight. 
Elsewhere, winds will more substantially overnight with 
seasonably cool low temperatures in the 50s.

Sunday: The axis of the now positively-tilted shortwave will
cross from British Columbia to Alberta Sunday and be supplanted
by a mid/upper level ridge moving onshore. Winds will not be as
breezy as previous days with a lower component of onshore flow,
though high temperatures should still be within a couple of 
degrees of Saturday's given the minimal change of airmass. /pmp

Monday through Friday: An upper-level ridge will amplify from the 
Four Corners into the Northern Rockies early next week, while an 
upper-level low over the Gulf of Alaska transitions eastward into 
British Columbia by mid-week. Good model agreement places the Inland 
Northwest under the influence of this subtle ridging and 
southwesterly flow aloft through Tuesday. Temperatures will trend 
much warmer with widespread highs in the 90s on Tuesday. This will 
result in widespread Moderate (Orange) HeatRisk, which is a level of 
heat that affects those who are sensitive to heat, especially folks 
without adequate cooling or hydration.  

In addition to the warming temperatures, this period will be 
highlighted by fire weather conditions. First, the southwesterly 
flow aloft will advect mid-level moisture northward into the Inland 
Northwest Monday night through Tuesday night, focusing primarily 
over southeast Washington and the southern Idaho Panhandle. Model 
soundings indicate elevated instability and mid-level moisture 
overtop a dry boundary layer. However, forecast confidence remains 
low. NBM probabilities for thunderstorms range from 5-15% over the 
Camas Prairie Monday night, increasing to 10-20% across southeast 
Washington and the southern Panhandle on Tuesday.

Second, ensembles have come into better agreement with the Gulf of 
Alaska low to move into British Columbia between Tuesday and 
Wednesday, with a trailing dry cold front pushing through the 
Pacific Northwest. There remains some uncertainty in the exact 
timing of this front, with models trending toward the front moving 
onshore the PNW Tuesday night or early Wednesday morning and 
shifting east of the Cascades Wednesday afternoon. Ahead of the 
front, strengthening cross-Cascade pressure gradients will result in 
elevated to critical fire weather conditions across central 
Washington late Tuesday afternoon and evening. NBM guidance is 
giving central Washington a 40-70% chance of relative humidity 
dropping below 20% combined with sustained winds above 15 mph. Fire 
weather concerns expand eastward on Wednesday as the dry front 
passes and a surface low deepens over southern Alberta. Despite 
modest post-frontal cooling, NBM guidance shows a 30-50% chance of 
relative humidity dropping below 20% combined with sustained winds 
above 15 mph across the lowlands of central and eastern Washington.

Synoptic uncertainty increases Thursday into Friday. About 55% of 
global ensemble members favor the ridge to immediately  
with rebounding temperatures late in the week. Conversely, the 
remaining 45% depict varying degrees of troughing, which would 
support more seasonal, although still warm temperatures. /vmt
